historic_survey.note: The 1968 Here Today survey was adopted by the Board of Supervisors under Resolution No. 268-70, so Planning counts the buildings it lists as individual historic resources. The 1976 city architectural survey rated buildings 0 to 5, 5 highest, and was never adopted as a register of historic resources. The 2017 Eureka Valley context statement names the house as a surviving property associated with agricultural production, and recommends a thematic survey of the agricultural survivals in the former western neighbourhoods of the city on the strength of it and the dwelling at 225-227 Eureka Street.

building.completed_conflict: The assessor's roll gives 1900; the 2017 Corbett Heights context statement dates the building to 1867.
building.name: Miller-Joost House

historical_record.description: Adam Miller built the first section of the house on his milk-ranch property, bought in 1868 from the Pioche & Robinson subdivision of 1867 and described as on the south side of Corbett Road near Eighteenth Street.
Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 79, the Miller-Joost House.
